beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: You think Apple only earns from iPhones? It doesn't. Here's why.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Google paid Apple $20B in one year, for one setting. Here's what it buys.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: That much money, for one setting? Which setting is worth it?

actions.name: Default search engine
actions.line: The one the phone asks first

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The search box. Type anything into Safari, the iPhone's browser, and Google answers first.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: But Google search is free. How does paying for it make sense?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Because every search shows ads, and a shop pays Google each time someone taps one.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So what does that one deal cost Google every day?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Spread over a year, that's $54.8M a day, and $2.3M every hour.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: But here's the twist. It isn't a flat fee at all. Apple keeps 36% of the ad money Google makes from Safari searches.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So every time I search on my iPhone, Apple gets a cut?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Every search that shows an ad. Google isn't paying for a setting. It's renting your habit, and the rent comes to $38,052 every minute.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Still think Apple only earns from iPhones? So, would you change your search box?
